terms.gloss: manifold, of many parts; many-sided; many times as great
evidence: Cic. N.D. 2.136: alvus est multiplex et tortuōsa (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 7.8.1: multiplex gaudium, a joy many times greater (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of what has many folds, layers or parts (armour, a bark, a feast of many dishes), and of a many-sided or changeable character (Cic.). For “multiple” meaning simply “many, more than one”, Latin says multī or complūrēs (see many).

phrases.latin: est magnum illud quidem vērum tamen multiplex puerī ingenium; quō ego regendō habeō negōtī satis
phrases.english: the boy has a great nature, it’s true, but a complicated one, and steering it keeps me busy enough

sources: Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cicero-epistulae), checked against the editions named there.
Citations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j).
